# TypeScript pipeline audit — September 4, 2026

The pipeline mixed ordinary PR validation, paid integration tests, preview publication, compatibility matrices, and releases. Release state depended on branch names, commit messages, pending changesets, Git tags, and npm metadata, without one consistent ordering.

This audit covers the repository at `08bbc7a1d` and recent GitHub Actions runs. Python job definitions and the Python release workflow are outside the rewrite.

## Findings and disposition

| Priority | Finding                                                                                                                                                                            | Disposition                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| High     | Stable publishing pulled `main` after the build. Canary tagging pulled `canary` after publication. Built code, published manifests, and tags could refer to different revisions.   | Resolve the branch once under the release lock; do not pull after building. Tag the built or originally published source revision.                                                                                                     |
| High     | Stable and canary publication had different concurrency groups despite sharing packages and dist-tags. Stable release also force-reset canary to main.                             | One non-cancelling release queue for both channels; remove automatic canary reset. Merge stable versions back through a PR.                                                                                                            |
| High     | Canary retry required pending changesets, although the version commit had already consumed them. A partial publication could be skipped on retry.                                  | Inspect registry state before deciding whether versioning or publication is needed. Recover unpushed tags from npm's `gitHead`.                                                                                                        |
| High     | Packaging and publishing could execute build hooks that modify another package's output. Existing fixes disabled npm publish hooks, but the final artifact path remained indirect. | Pack every public package before upload, disable lifecycle hooks, validate entry points and integrity, smoke-test those tarballs, then publish those files sequentially. Add a regression test with a destructive client prepack hook. |
| High     | Stable publication relied on matching a specific commit message or `force_publish`.                                                                                                | Publish based on versioned manifests and registry state; use a stable version PR, independent of commit titles.                                                                                                                        |
| High     | Verification ran before canary versioning and its second build.                                                                                                                    | Verify the final versioned artifacts, after one build.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Medium   | `.railway-deploy-marker` was hidden. Upload-artifact defaults can exclude hidden files. A successful release could omit the artifact that enables downstream work.                 | Use `railway-deploy-marker.txt`; include source SHA and exact scaffold/SDK versions.                                                                                                                                                   |
| Medium   | PR CI rebuilt the complete workspace in multiple jobs and exposed OpenAI credentials to an agent integration step.                                                                 | One build and package-test job without API secrets; a separate manual paid integration workflow.                                                                                                                                       |
| Medium   | A generator change launched a 30-job compatibility matrix on an ordinary PR.                                                                                                       | Manual scaffold compatibility workflow; keep generator unit tests in normal CI.                                                                                                                                                        |
| Medium   | Every matching PR published previews, with pnpm 10 against a pnpm 11 workspace.                                                                                                    | Require `ci:preview` on a same-repository PR; align pnpm and use a frozen lockfile.                                                                                                                                                    |
| Medium   | Claude subscribed to every review/review-comment event. GitHub could require approval before its mention filter was evaluated.                                                     | Only maintainer `@claude` conversation comments invoke it. Remove review-event subscriptions.                                                                                                                                          |
| Medium   | Inspector E2E jobs were permanently disabled, had an incorrect `all` matrix expression, and used stale pnpm versions.                                                              | Enable explicit manual execution; repair the expression and TypeScript setup. Preserve the Python job definition.                                                                                                                      |
| Medium   | Scaffold smoke tests slept, ignored process failures, and reported success. Post-release tests resolved mutable `canary` tags rather than the completed release's versions.        | Require observable readiness; pass exact scaffold/SDK versions from the verified release marker.                                                                                                                                       |
| Medium   | Docker publication was keyed by run SHA, allowing competing `latest` writes. It inferred the release revision from `workflow_run.head_sha`.                                        | Serialize Docker publication and read the verified source revision from the marker.                                                                                                                                                    |
| Low      | Scheduled SDK evals and synthesis had no overlap control. Synthesis interpolated a manual input into shell text.                                                                   | Add concurrency limits and pass the window through an environment variable. Keep their schedules.                                                                                                                                      |

## What the recent runs show

The last six inspected SDK eval runs were all `schedule` events on `main`. Neither the eval workflow nor synthesis has a PR trigger. Ordinary CI did contain a separate native OpenAI integration test; these are distinct sources of AI spending.

Recent Claude runs such as [33921637045](https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use/actions/runs/33921637045) ended with `action_required` on `pull_request_review_comment`. Other conversation-comment runs were skipped. This supports an approval/event-noise explanation; it does not establish that every historical Claude failure had the same cause.

In [canary release 33815924436](https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use/actions/runs/33815924436), Changesets reported CLI, Inspector, and server versions published successfully. The subsequent verification continued to report `mcp-use@2.4.3-canary.0` missing and its canary tag unchanged. This shows why publish-command success cannot replace registry verification. These logs do not prove the precise cause of the user's earlier client artifact incident.

The next inspected canary release and the latest stable release succeeded. The rewrite preserves the existing channel-regression and artifact-content checks rather than treating every observed failure as a reason to remove validation.

## Rollout and remaining boundaries

- The changes are local and reviewable. No package was published, workflow dispatched, live label created, branch rule modified, or deployment started during the audit.
- The inspected active default-branch ruleset requires review and linear history but does not list required status checks. Decide which new check names to require before relying on merge protection. The normal TypeScript job now reports through the reusable **TypeScript checks** workflow.
- Let existing release runs finish before merging this rewrite: runs using the old per-branch concurrency groups do not share the new lock.
- npm OIDC publishing must remain configured for `typescript-release.yml`. A credentialed publish was deliberately not part of local validation. Verify the first canary release in GitHub before stable promotion.
- Actionlint 1.7.12 rejects GitHub's newer `concurrency.queue` key. Validation suppresses that exact diagnostic, supported by GitHub's [queue documentation](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-05-07-github-actions-concurrency-groups-now-allow-larger-queues/). The untouched documentation workflow also has a pre-existing deprecated Python action diagnostic.
- `docs.yml` still combines Python and TypeScript API generation. Splitting its Python work was excluded from this migration.
- `approve-fork-pr.yml` still supports maintainer-approved Python runs and inherits the secrets those Python jobs use. Its TypeScript callee receives no secrets. Changing the Python approval model is outside scope.
- `sync-inspector.yml`, Dependabot changesets, labels, stale issues, links, reusable version bumping, and notification testing remain separate repository-maintenance workflows. They are not additional SDK eval triggers.
- Multi-package publication is not atomic. Dependency-first uploads and post-publication verification reduce failure modes, but consumers can observe a partly completed release. Recover a failed release before merging further package changes into that channel.

## Local verification

The workspace installed with pnpm 11.13.1 and the frozen lockfile. The complete workspace build passed. All seven public packages packed successfully and passed declared-entry-point checks. The clean installation smoke test passed with those exact tarballs, including runtime imports, production build, and dev/start readiness.

All 24 release-tool tests pass. They cover channel constraints, partial publication, unexpected tag changes, dependency ordering, tarball tampering, source recovery, refusing later unversioned source, and disabled prepack hooks. Workflow syntax and Python-job invariants are checked separately. See the change summary for final test counts and any remaining failures.

Final package results: client 347 passed; server 475 passed; agent 139 passed and 1 skipped; Inspector 267 passed; tunnel 13 passed; scaffolder 28 passed. CLI proxy/packing tests passed (3), and its Vitest suite reported 284 passed and 12 failed. All 12 failures are timeouts in `tests/cli/dev.test.ts` around file reload and watcher behavior. A focused rerun with `CHOKIDAR_USEPOLLING=true` reproduced the same 12 failures. Their cause is unresolved; no product source or test expectations were changed to hide them. The new CI continues to run these checks, so this audit does not claim an entirely green package suite.

## PR changesets and release-doc readiness follow-up

The previous `typescript-changeset-check` job excluded ordinary PRs targeting canary (`github.base_ref != 'canary'`) and printed a warning instead of failing when no changeset was present. The initial rewrite also omitted that check. The restored check now runs before the build on both target branches, uses the exact PR base SHA, propagates that base through approved fork runs, and executes the Changesets CLI even when the changeset directory is empty. Intentional no-release package changes use an empty changeset. Only trusted promotion and bot version PRs get the consumed-changeset exception.

Stable promotion now requires changed, nonempty documentation entries for the projected release versions. TypeScript and Inspector notes are validated separately. Stable preparation and publication recheck the docs; canary prerelease publication is unchanged. Regression tests exercise the real Changesets CLI against temporary Git histories and verify changelog versions, routing, stale/empty/duplicate entries, and inherited notes on the version PR.
